graph.summary: Insulin Human → Insulin receptor → glucose import → Hyperglycemia → Diabetes mellitus type 1

evidence.snippet: Its binding to insulin receptor on the surface of diverse cells allows glucose entry into cells, and activates a variety of cellular actions.
evidence.explanation: Insulin binds directly to the insulin receptor (INSR/UniProt:P06213) on cell surfaces; this molecular interaction is the initiating event of the insulin signalling cascade that lowers blood glucose.

evidence.snippet: activated the insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS1)/phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signaling pathway, and enhanced the translocation of glucose transporter type 4 (GLUT4) and glucose uptake in adipocytes treated with palmitic acid.
evidence.explanation: Insulin receptor activation triggers the IRS1/PI3K/AKT cascade that drives GLUT4 translocation to the plasma membrane, thereby positively regulating glucose import (GO:0046323) into insulin-sensitive cells.

paper.title: Esculin ameliorates obesity-induced insulin resistance by improving adipose tissue remodeling and activating the IRS1/PI3K/AKT/GLUT4 pathway.

evidence.snippet: impairments in the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT signaling pathway, or perturbations in the trafficking of glucose transporters (GLUTs), which mediate the uptake of glucose into cells.
evidence.explanation: The PI3K/AKT pathway downstream of INSR controls GLUT trafficking and glucose uptake into cells; disruption of this pathway impairs glucose import, confirming INSR positively regulates GO:0046323.

paper.title: Glucose Transporters in Diabetic Kidney Disease-Friends or Foes?

evidence.snippet: promoted glucose uptake in the liver and skeletal muscle, and upregulated hepatic Ghr and Igf1 levels to facilitate glucose homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Promoting cellular glucose import in liver and muscle facilitates glucose homeostasis, the inverse of hyperglycemia; the same study showed that this effect alleviated hyperglycemia in insulin-deficient models, confirming that glucose import (GO:0046323) is negatively correlated with hyperglycemia (HP:0003074).

paper.title: The novel adipokine Placin regulates glucose homeostasis via insulin secretion and IGF1 receptor signaling.
paper.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

evidence.snippet: In T1DM, the destruction of pancreatic β-cells leads to reduced insulin production or even absolute insulin deficiency, which consequently results in hyperglycemia.
evidence.explanation: Hyperglycemia is directly caused by the insulin deficiency that results from autoimmune beta-cell destruction in T1DM; it is therefore a manifestation of the disease.

paper.title: Molecular imaging of β-cells: diabetes and beyond.

evidence.snippet: The autoimmune process leads to a deficiency in insulin production and resultant hyperglycemia requiring lifelong treatment with insulin administration.
evidence.explanation: This clinical review confirms that hyperglycemia is a direct manifestation of T1DM caused by autoimmune insulin deficiency, and that insulin administration is the required treatment.

paper.title: Immune Intervention and Preservation of Pancreatic Beta Cell Function in Type 1 Diabetes.
